title: Cold rebuild: what will Git record?
summary: Fix a commit message draft with real Vim and commit it cleanly with real Git, from memory.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a skill stuck. In *Servers, sudo, diffs and git* you fixed a commit message draft with real Vim and
committed it so Git recorded exactly the message you meant. Now do it again from memory: the same scenario, **no
hints, no solution to peek at**. The checks are exactly the ones you passed the first time.
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. If you get stuck, go back to the lesson, then try
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

steps.prompt: Why does `:w !sudo tee %` work when `:w` failed?
options: vim itself still runs as you; it only hands the text to `tee`, which runs as root via sudo and writes the file
steps.explain: `%` expands to the file name; the writing process is `tee`, not vim.

steps.title: What will Git record? Cold
prompt: In `~/repo` a fix is staged, and `~/COMMIT_DRAFT` holds its message with a typo (`Fxi`) and Git's `#` help lines.
Fix the typo with Vim from the command line, then commit with that file so the recorded message has no `#` lines.
From memory: no hints this time.
